metadata.title: RAG Explained for Product Managers
metadata.greeting_note: Presenter: Vineet S.. Closing card: MedhavyOutro (toolkit defaults).
metadata.note: 9:16 Short (about one minute). Native portrait scenes; not a crop of the long video.

beats.narration_text: Hello, I'm Vineet S.. A language model knows a lot, but not your company's documents. R A G fixes that.

props.command: What is RAG and why do companies use it?
output: Your data, the model's language skills

beats.narration_text: R A G has four steps. Chunk and index your documents. Retrieve the passages that match the question. Augment the prompt with them. Then generate an answer grounded in those passages.

layers.title: 1  Chunk and index
layers.sub: Split documents into passages and index them

layers.title: 2  Retrieve
layers.sub: Find passages closest to the question

layers.title: 3  Augment
layers.sub: Put those passages into the prompt

layers.title: 4  Generate
layers.sub: The model answers using them, with citations

beats.narration_text: Why do companies use it? Fresh information. Private company data. Fewer hallucinations. Citations users can check. It is cheaper than retraining. And it respects access control.
The product manager owns four decisions. What data goes in. How to split it. How many passages to retrieve. And what to say when nothing is found.

layers.title: How to split it
layers.sub: Passage size changes what is found

layers.title: How many passages
layers.sub: Too few miss, too many distract
